density_dependence_reading: The pooled Spearman of phantom count against atoms per cell has OPPOSITE SIGNS at two views (+0.4571) and three views (-0.1471), so a single rate would misreport it. Decomposing resolves the sign flip. Conditional on Phi_0 being nonempty, count rises steeply with atoms per cell at both view counts (rho 0.8331 at two views, n=1408; rho 0.8273 at three, n=365). What differs is the probability of being nonempty at all: flat in atoms at two views (rho 0.0299, p = 0.19) but DECREASING at three (rho -0.1875, p = 6.9e-17). The three-view pooled negative is therefore a mixture effect - larger cells are less likely to admit any phantom under three-view verification, but produce many when they do - and not evidence that density protects against phantoms. This is the measurement the method section promises in place of a proved rate; we report the decomposition rather than a single coefficient.
note_on_binned_means: The binned means at three views (2.143, 0.530, 10.135, 5.083 across 0-20, 20-40, 40-60, 60-100 atoms) are non-monotone because only 18.72% of structures have any phantom at three views, so each bin mean is dominated by zeros and a few large counts. The conditional statistics above are the interpretable form; the bin means are reported for completeness only.
